label: Kimi K3.1 Pro
output:
Used Kilbarrack Van Co on Saturday 17 October for a move from Phibsborough to Drumcondra. It was a two-bed flat, although mostly my own stuff, and the new place is a fourth-floor walk-up with no lift, so it wasn’t the easiest job. Booking through the website was straightforward and I paid the €50 deposit by Revolut.

The quote was €340 for up to four hours, with two lads and the van, and the move took about three and a half hours. I’d had other quotes of €450 and upwards, so it was comfortably the best value I found.

They were due at 9am and arrived at 10:30. I did get a text at 8:40 saying their previous job had overrun, which I appreciated, but it still left me sitting on boxes with a coffee going cold. It wasn’t the end of the world for me because I had a bit of flexibility, but it’s worth allowing extra time if you’re working around a strict landlord handover or need to be out by a particular hour. To be fair, Dessie knocked €40 off afterwards because of the lateness, without me even asking, which was decent of him.

Once they arrived, the lads worked hard and were good to deal with. The couch wouldn’t go around the turn on the third-floor stairs, and one of the lads — Kev, I think — produced an Allen key from his pocket, took the legs off and got it straight in. That bit of quick thinking saved a lot of hassle. They also put my bed back together without being asked and took away a flat-pack shelf I didn’t want, both of which I really appreciated after a long day of moving.

The one thing I was properly disappointed about was my brass floor lamp. The base got chipped during the move. Most things were wrapped in blankets, but the lamp wasn’t, and because it was my nanny’s it has sentimental value beyond what it would cost to replace. I was a bit gutted about that, so I wouldn’t leave it out of a review. My advice to anyone moving would be to point out anything fragile, awkward or sentimental beforehand and specifically ask for it to be wrapped — or wrap it yourself for peace of mind. And to the lads: wrap the lamps!

Overall, four stars feels fair. Good value, hard workers, helpful with the awkward furniture and the couple of extra jobs, and Dessie dealt with the delay fairly. It’s not five because they were an hour and a half late and the lamp got damaged, but I would use them again. I’d just leave myself a bigger time buffer and make sure anything precious was well protected before they arrived.
